To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) different network sampling algorithms may yield networks with similar network metrics and (b) alternative algorithms for the generation of networks with the same network metrics may yield networks with different network metrics.

(1) different network sampling algorithms for the same network type can generate networks with similar connectivity pattern; and (2) the alternative algorithms for a specific network sampling type can generate networks that are different from the networks generated by the algorithm that is most popularly used in the literature.

(1) the connectivity patterns that are associated with a given set of values of network metrics are not unique, (2) alternative network sampling algorithms that are designed to produce the same connectivity pattern may yield networks with different network metrics, and (3) the same network sampling algorithm may yield networks with the same network metrics but different connectivity patterns.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the extent to which the connectivity patterns of networks are represented by a limited set of popular network measures.
the extent to which the full features of network connectivity patterns are preserved in the process of network sampling.
a better understanding of network sampling and classification algorithms, and their implications for network data analyses.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the network sampling algorithms are effective in generating networks with desired network features.
a specific network sampling algorithm is not a substitute for a specific network model.
the connectivity pattern of a network cannot be inferred from a limited number of network metrics.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the connectivity patterns of networks generated from different network sampling algorithms are not the same.
the connectivity patterns of simulated networks can be quite different from the connectivity patterns that the algorithm is aiming for.
the network sampling algorithms are not as precise as one would hope.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the choice of network sampling algorithm is crucial to the validity of conclusions drawn from a simulated network study.
the network model representation of a network is not a simple one-to-one mapping from a set of network metrics.

network sampling algorithms can generate a wide variety of connectivity patterns, and that these connectivity patterns are not necessarily the same as the ones that the sampling algorithm aims to create.
